cues.en: A few years ago, I made the world's first homemade silicon chip in my garage fab. I just made version two, which has 100 transistors on it, and they're smaller, better, and faster than the old one. I made an array of 12 of these, so that's 1,200
cues.zh: 几年前，我在自家车库工厂里造出了世界上第一块自制硅芯片。我刚做出了第二版，上面有100个晶体管，比旧版更小、更好、更快。我做了由12个这种芯片组成的阵列，所以就是1,200

cues.en: transistors on the same piece of silicon. Intel's first processor had only 2,000 transistors, so we're already approaching a decent level of complexity, and I should be able to make some really interesting circuits out of this soon. I did some cool projects with my first chip, like a LED flasher and a guitar distortion pedal. They worked really well, but needed one or two nine volt batteries attached to them because the threshold voltage of the old MOSFETs were really high.
cues.zh: 个晶体管在同一块硅片上。Intel的第一款处理器只有2,000个晶体管，所以我们已经接近相当不错的复杂度了，而且我应该很快就能用它做出一些非常有趣的电路。我用第一块芯片做了一些很酷的项目，比如LED闪烁器和吉他失真踏板。它们运行得很好，但需要接上一两节9伏电池，因为旧MOSFET的阈值电压非常高。

cues.en: This new chip is made on a polysilicon gate process.
cues.zh: 这块新芯片采用多晶硅栅工艺制造。

cues.en: All these details are on the write up on my blog, but the effect of that is that they work well at very low voltages. They have a threshold voltage of only about one volt, and that means that I can power them, off of three point three and five volt logic levels. They draw less power, and I should be able to pack more of them into a smaller die area.
cues.zh: 所有细节都写在我博客的文章里，但这样做的效果是它们能在非常低的电压下良好工作。它们的阈值电压只有大约1伏，这意味着我可以用3.3伏和5伏的逻辑电平给它们供电。它们耗电更少，而且我应该能把更多晶体管塞进更小的晶片面积里。

cues.en: For simple chips like this, the process actually starts in Photoshop.
cues.zh: 对于这样简单的芯片，工艺其实从Photoshop开始。

cues.en: There's only four layers to design, and it's easier to use this than to use some more complicated software.
cues.zh: 只有四层需要设计，用这个比用一些更复杂的软件更容易。

cues.en: I start with a lot of 200 millimeter wafers that have some pretty specific starting parameters. They're way too big, so I dice them up using a diamond scribe into smaller bits. I normally do about half inch squares like this, but I can process larger things up to about two inch wafers.
cues.zh: 我从很多 200 毫米晶圆开始，它们有一些相当具体的初始参数。它们太大了，所以我就用金刚石划刀把它们切成更小的块。我通常切成像这样大约半英寸见方的小块，但我也能处理更大的东西，最大到大约两英寸的晶圆。

cues.en: The first layer to define is the doped layer that makes the source and drains for the MOSFETs. I put it on this homemade spin coater, and then I deposit photoresist on top of it. You only need about a 100 microliters or so to cover a small wafer like this, and we spin it at 4,000 RPM for thirty seconds.
cues.zh: 首先要定义的第一层是掺杂层，它用来形成 MOSFET 的源极和漏极。我把它放到这台自制的旋涂机上，然后在上面沉积光刻胶。像这样的小晶圆，只需要大约 100 微升就能覆盖，我们以 4,000 RPM 旋转 30 秒。

cues.en: After all the excess photoresist has been spun off, it's dried on a hot plate at about 95 degrees c for one minute. This drives off the rest of the solvents and, leaves us with a solid film.
cues.zh: 等多余的光刻胶都被甩掉后，在约 95 摄氏度的热板上烘干一分钟。这会驱除剩余的溶剂，并留下一层固态薄膜。

cues.en: The result is a beautiful looking and uniform covering of the whole wafer.
cues.zh: 结果是整个晶圆上覆盖着一层漂亮又均匀的薄膜。

cues.en: Then it's off to the homebuilt maskless photolithography stepper for exposure. The basic idea is that we load up an image on this laptop that we wanna project onto the chip. Then there's a standard DLP projector and some optics that shoot that down and reduce it onto the wafer. I have a whole video on this tool, so I recommend checking that out. In the center, you see a little blue dot. That's the entire exposure field. It lasts about nine seconds, then the blue goes away at the end of the exposure, we can step the wafer to another location and expose that part too.
cues.zh: 然后就送去用自制的无掩模光刻步进机进行曝光。基本思路是，我们在这台笔记本上加载一张想投影到芯片上的图像。然后有一个标准 DLP 投影仪和一些光学系统，把图像向下投射并缩小到晶圆上。我有一整期视频专门讲这个工具，推荐去看看。在中心，你能看到一个小蓝点。那就是整个曝光场。曝光持续大约九秒，然后蓝点在曝光结束时消失；接着我们可以把晶圆步进到另一个位置，把那一部分也曝光。

cues.en: Just like processing film in a darkroom, the next step is development.
cues.zh: 就像在暗房里冲洗胶片一样，下一步是显影。

cues.en: I put it in a couple percent potassium hydroxide solution for about a minute, and this etches away the parts of the photoresist that were exposed because it's a positive photoresist.
cues.zh: 我把它放进几百合一的氢氧化钾溶液里大约一分钟，这会把光刻胶中曝光过的部分蚀刻掉，因为它是正性光刻胶。

cues.en: I wash it with water to get rid of the residual developer, and then we're ready to do the next step. I can put under a microscope to inspect it and make sure everything worked out well. If it didn't, you can always just strip off the photoresist layer and try again with maybe a different exposure or development time.
cues.zh: 我用水冲洗，去掉残留的显影液，然后就准备进行下一步了。我可以把它放到显微镜下检查，确保一切顺利。如果没成功，你随时可以剥掉光刻胶层，换个曝光或显影时间再试一次。

cues.en: Now that the image is formed in the photoresist, I transfer that into the underlying polysilicon layer using an etchant.
cues.zh: 现在图像已经在光刻胶中形成了，我用蚀刻剂把它转移到下面的多晶硅层。

cues.en: Once it's etched, we don't need the photoresist mask layer anymore, that can be stripped off using acetone.
cues.zh: 蚀刻完成后，我们就不再需要光刻胶掩膜层了，可以用丙酮把它剥掉。

cues.en: The wafer is then cleaned and dried, and we spin on a dopant.
cues.zh: 然后清洗并干燥晶圆，再旋涂掺杂剂。

cues.en: This is a phosphorus solution that's suspended in a liquid silicon dioxide.
cues.zh: 这是一种悬浮在液态二氧化硅中的磷溶液。

cues.en: This is spun on just like the photoresist, and then we bake it at very high temperature, over 1,000 degrees C, for about forty five minutes. This drives in the phosphorus atoms into the little wells that we just defined using lithography,
cues.zh: 它就像光刻胶一样旋涂上去，然后在超过1000摄氏度的高温下烘烤大约四十五分钟。这会把磷原子驱入我们刚刚用光刻定义的小坑里，

cues.en: and that basically forms the source and drains of the MOSFETs.
cues.zh: 这基本上就形成了MOSFET的源极和漏极。

cues.en: I have to push it into the center of the furnace using this quartz rod, and then at the end of the process, we pull it out the other side. The process of spin coating photoresist, baking it, exposing it, and developing it, is then repeated exactly twice, once for the gate layer and then again for the contact.
cues.zh: 我得用这根石英棒把它推入炉子中心，然后在工艺结束时从另一侧拉出来。旋涂光刻胶、烘烤、曝光、显影的流程随后要精确重复两次，一次用于栅极层，再一次用于接触层。

cues.en: The gate is etched just like we did before, with the polysilicon etchant, and the contact layer has to be etched as well because now after the high temperature step, there's a layer of silicon dioxide insulating everything. So after the contact mask is formed, you have to use something like hydrofluoric acid or,
cues.zh: 栅极像之前一样用多晶硅刻蚀剂刻蚀，接触层也必须刻蚀，因为高温步骤之后，有一层二氧化硅把所有东西绝缘了。所以接触掩模形成后，得用氢氟酸之类的东西，或者，

cues.en: CHF three reactive ion etching to get rid of that insulator so we can make good electrical contact.
cues.zh: 用 CHF3 反应离子刻蚀去掉这层绝缘体，才能形成良好的电接触。

cues.en: Then we stick the wafer into a vacuum chamber to either sputter or thermally evaporate metal. I'm evaporating aluminum, a thick layer of, about a micron or so. And then we do the whole photolithography
cues.zh: 然后把晶圆放进真空腔，溅射或热蒸发金属。我蒸发的是铝，厚厚一层，大约一微米左右。然后我们再做整套光刻

cues.en: process again of spin coating and exposing and developing to define that metal layer.
cues.zh: 工艺，再次进行旋涂、曝光和显影，来定义那层金属。

cues.en: Once that's done, stick the wafer into a warm phosphoric acid bath that etches off the residual aluminum and finally the chip is done.
cues.zh: 完成后，把晶圆放进温热的磷酸浴，刻蚀掉残留铝，芯片终于完成。

cues.en: At this point, I'll inspect the chip pretty thoroughly and take a lot of close-up pictures to measure parameters like gate length and width and layer thicknesses if I do a cross section. I can put it on the probe station, which has a bunch of really small tungsten needles and allow me to make connections directly to the transistors. Transistors. It's very finicky, and these transistors are so small that it's not actually that, trivial to make contact to them. But, anyway, I boot up all this test equipment that allows me to, characterize them. I do a little bit of programming to define the kind of tests I want to do, and then, hopefully, we're we're greeted with this great curve. So this is the
cues.zh: 到这一步，我会比较彻底地检查芯片，拍很多特写照片；如果做横截面，就测量栅长、栅宽和层厚等参数。我可以把它放到探针台上，上面有很多非常小的钨针，让我能直接连到晶体管。晶体管。这很麻烦，这些晶体管太小了，要和它们接触其实并不那么简单。不过总之，我启动所有这些测试设备，好对它们进行表征。我写一点程序来定义想做的测试类型，然后希望能看到这条很棒的曲线。所以这是

cues.en: ID versus VDS curve of an n channel MOSFET.
cues.zh: 一个 n 沟道 MOSFET 的 ID 对 VDS 曲线。

cues.en: Here's an ideal one, taken off of the Internet, and then here's the one that I'm getting from my FETs, and they look great.
cues.zh: 这是一个理想的例子，我从网上找来的；这是我用 FET 做出来的，它们看起来很不错。

cues.en: I hope you found that interesting and enjoyed learning about my second integrated circuit. I got a bunch of requests to set up a Patreon or something like that. I'm not sure if that's the best way to do it, but I'll put a link in the description if you want to support more homebrew semiconductor fabrication experiments like this. Thanks for watching.
cues.zh: 希望你觉得这很有趣，也喜欢了解我的第二块集成电路。很多人要求我开个 Patreon 之类的。我不确定这是不是最好的方式，但如果你想支持更多这样的自制半导体制造实验，我会在简介里放一个链接。感谢观看。
